'''''Alisma gramineum''''' is a small [[aquatic plant]] in the [[Alismataceae|water-plantain]] family. It has several common names including '''narrowleaf water-plantain''', '''ribbonleaf water-plantain''' or '''ribbon-leaved water-plantain''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''grass-leaved water-plantain'''. It grows in mud or submerged in shallow [[Freshwater|fresh]] or [[brackish water]] in [[marsh]]y areas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=ALGR|title=Plants Profile for Alisma gramineum (narrowleaf water plantain)|website=plants.usda.gov|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref>

==Description==
The leaves and tiny purple-tinted white flowers may be submersed or not. When the flowers grow underwater they are [[Cleistogamy|cleistogamous]], meaning they stay closed and self-pollinate. When the flowers grow above water they open. The leaves above the surface are stiff and wide, but submerged leaves are ribbon-like. The fruit is a ring of dry [[nutlet]]s. Reproduction is by seed or from division of the [[corm]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?7883,7884,7885|title=UC/JEPS: Jepson Manual treatment for ALISMA gramineum|website=ucjeps.berkeley.edu|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Alisma gramineum'' is widespread across temperate and subarctic portions of [[Asia]] and [[Europe]] and [[North Africa]] from [[France]] and [[Libya]] to [[China]] and [[Yakutsk]]. It is reported from much of [[Canada]] from [[British Columbia]] to [[Quebec]], as well as most of the western [[United States]] plus [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Vermont]] and [[Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=294793|title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|website=apps.kew.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Alisma%20gramineum.png Biota of North America Program]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=alisma+gramineum|title=Alisma gramineum [Mestolaccia sottile]|website=luirig.altervista.org|language=it|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200024710|title=Alisma gramineum in Flora of China @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref> This is an endangered and protected species in the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ukbap.org.uk/UKPlans.aspx?ID=83 |title=UK Action Plan |access-date=2007-10-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071028111442/http://www.ukbap.org.uk/UKPlans.aspx?ID=83 |archive-date=2007-10-28 }}</ref> It was first found in Britain in [[Worcestershire]] in 1920, and later beside the [[River Glen, Lincolnshire|River Glen]] in [[Lincolnshire]].{{citation needed|date=March 2020}} At both sites, populations are small, and vary in size from year to year.{{citation needed|date=March 2020}} It typically grows in shallow, nutrient-rich water at the edge of bodies of water and fenland drains. It is an annual plant, or a short-lived perennial, and the seeds may remain viable for some years, sometimes germinating after the ground has been disturbed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/alisma-gramineum |title=''Alisma gramineum'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |access-date=2020-03-13 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
